home_info.about_me:
I am an Associate Professor in the Department of Economics at the University of Copenhagen. I am a member of the Center for Economic Behavior and Inequality (CEBI), a Research Fellow at CESifo, a Research Fellow at IZA@LISER, and a Research Fellow at RFBerlin. I received my B.A. in Economics from Bogazici University in 2003, and my Ph.D. in Economics from University of Maryland, College Park in 2009.

My research lies at the intersection of health economics and labor economics. I use population-wide administrative data and quasi-experimental designs to study how health, health care, and social policies shape people’s health and socioeconomic outcomes. My work focuses on four broad themes: the effects of medical care, health care access, and provider quality; the consequences of health shocks for families and intergenerational inequality; the determinants and consequences of mental health across the life course; and violence and victimization among vulnerable populations. Across these areas, I am interested in how public policy can reduce health and socioeconomic inequalities.

I currently serve as an editor at Journal of Health Economics (2025-).
